labrujasuchus:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

labrujasuchus:study:1.title: A new shuvosaurid (Archosauria, Poposauroidea) from the Late Triassic (Norian) Hayden Quarry of New Mexico, U.S.A. (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically the Norian age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Triassic (Norian)

facts.statement: The type locality for Labrujasuchus is the Chinle Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Chinle Formation

facts.statement: Fossils of Labrujasuchus have been found in the United States.
facts.quote: Country: United States

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus was discovered in the region of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Region: New Mexico

facts.statement: The genus Labrujasuchus was described by Turner and colleagues.
facts.quote: Authors: Turner et al.

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus represents a new genus and new species.
facts.quote: Novelty: Gen. et sp. nov

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton of Labrujasuchus was discovered in 2006.
facts.quote: Labrujasuchus was described based on a partial skeleton discovered in 2006

facts.statement: The holotype of Labrujasuchus was collected from the Hayden Quarry at Ghost Ranch.
facts.quote: The holotype has been collected from the Hayden Quarry at Ghost Ranch

facts.statement: The holotype comes from paleochannel H2, which is dated to approximately 211 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Member is divided into three distinct paleochannels, labeled H4, H2 and H3, with the holotype of Labrujasuchus coming from H2, which has been dated to the mid Norian (ca. 211 Mya)

facts.statement: Researchers referred additional fossils, including a left coracoid from channel H3 and a left tibia from channel H4, to Labrujasuchus.
facts.quote: Turner and colleagues subsequently referred a number of other Hayden Quarry shuvosaurid fossils to Labrujasuchus, including a left coracoid from H3 and a left tibia from H4

facts.statement: The description of Labrujasuchus involved authors including Alan H. Turner, Ciara E. Kernan, Adam Laing, Adam C. Pritchard, Michelle R. Stocker, Randall B. Irmis, Nathan D. Smith, Sarah Werning, and Sterling J. Nesbitt.
facts.quote: Alan H. Turner, Ciara E. Kernan, Adam Laing, Adam C. Pritchard, Michelle R. Stocker, Randall B. Irmis, Nathan D. Smith, Sarah Werning, Sterling J. Nesbitt

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus is classified as a member of the family Shuvosauridae within the superfamily Poposauroidea.
facts.quote: A member of Poposauroidea belonging to the family Shuvosauridae

facts.statement: The genus name for this animal is Labrujasuchus.
facts.quote: genus: Labrujasuchus

facts.statement: The species name for this animal is expectatus.
facts.quote: species: expectatus

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus is known from a partial associated skeleton containing forelimb material, vertebrae, hindlimb parts, and pubic region elements.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial associated skeleton including forelimb material, a few vertebrae as well as parts of the hindlimbs and pubic region

facts.statement: The anatomy of Labrujasuchus closely resembles that of the North American shuvosaurids Effigia and Shuvosaurus.
facts.quote: The anatomy of Labrujasuchus closely resembles other North American shuvosaurids, namely Effigia and Shuvosaurus

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus possesses a large internal tuberosity on the humerus, sometimes called a medial process.
facts.quote: On the humerus Labrujasuchus presents a large internal tuberosity, referred to by some authors as a medial process

facts.statement: The head of the humerus in Labrujasuchus is teardrop-shaped rather than D-shaped.
facts.quote: the head of the humerus is best described as teardrop-shaped as opposed to D-shaped

facts.statement: Labrujasuchus has a hypertrophied ventral crest on the ischium, making the bone deeper than wide, unlike other North American shuvosaurids.
facts.quote: the hypertrophied ventral crest of the ischium, which makes the bone deeper than wide unlike in other North American shuvosaurids

facts.statement: An anterior groove on the fibula, located just medial to the iliofibularis trochanter, is a distinguishing feature of Labrujasuchus.
facts.quote: the presence of an anterior groove on the fibula just medial to the iliofibularis trochanter

facts.statement: The specific layer containing the holotype of Labrujasuchus is dated to the mid Norian, approximately 211 million years ago.
facts.quote: The Member is divided into three distinct paleochannels, labeled H4, H2 and H3, with the holotype of Labrujasuchus coming from H2, which has been dated to the mid Norian (ca. 211 Mya)

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Turner et al. excluded the coeval shuvosaurid Sonselasuchus, which was named two months before Labrujasuchus.
facts.quote: the family consists of four members, Sillosuchus from the Carnian of Argentina, as well as Labrujasuchus, Shuvosaurus, and Effigia, which are known from the southern United States. The analysis by Turner and colleagues did not include the coeval shuvosaurid Sonselasuchus, named two months prior to Labrujasuchus

rejected.statement: It is debated whether other remains found in the Hayden Quarry definitively belong to Labrujasuchus, as they have only been tentatively assigned to the taxon.
rejected.quote: a number of other remains found throughout the Hayden Quarry have also been tentatively assigned to this taxon
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Several neck vertebrae and a pair of ischia found in the quarry cannot be confidently assigned to the genus Labrujasuchus.
rejected.quote: several neck vertebrae and a pair of ischia that cannot be confidently assigned to the genus
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Several neck vertebrae and a pair of ischia'
